references.text: The Lord predicts that he will harden Pharaoh's heart, the same theme repeated here in 14:8
The Lord declares that he will harden Pharaoh's heart, a recurring motif in the story of the Exodus from Egypt
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he would not listen to Moses and Aaron, as the Lord had said
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart after the boil plague, using the same expression found in 14:8
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart after the locust plague
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he would not let the people go
The Lord predicts that he will harden Pharaoh's heart so that he pursues the Israelites, directly linking to verse 8
The Lord hardened the hearts of the Egyptians so that they pursued the Israelites into the sea
The Israelites went out with a raised hand from Egypt, using the same expression 'בְּיָד רָמָה' (with a raised hand) as in 14:8
The Lord brought Israel out of Egypt with a strong hand, referencing the Exodus from Egypt
The psalm praises the Lord for casting Pharaoh and his army into the Red Sea, the result of the pursuit mentioned in 14:8
Paul uses Pharaoh's hardening as an example of God's sovereign will and his right to harden whom he wills
Confirms the same theological cause (God's hardening) that prevented liberation at various stages of the events.
Uses Pharaoh's hardened heart as a historical and theological warning about God's power over human will.
Confirms that Pharaoh's stubbornness fulfilled God's prophecy to harden his heart.
Describes the final outcome of Pharaoh's pursuit (the sea), which began with his hardened heart.
